routes.name: Erie Canal, Albany to Buffalo
citations: Peter L. Bernstein, Wedding of the Waters: The Erie Canal and the Making of a Great Nation (New York: Norton, 2005)
routes.notes: Opened 26 October 1825. Our line through Schenectady, Utica, Syracuse, Rochester and Lockport.
routes.goods_source: general history; not from a cargo manifest
routes.citation: Peter L. Bernstein, Wedding of the Waters: The Erie Canal and the Making of a Great Nation (New York: Norton, 2005)
routes.history: The Erie Canal opened on 26 October 1825 and ran 363 miles (584 km) from Albany on the Hudson to Buffalo on Lake Erie. Critics called it 'Clinton's Ditch', but the legislature approved $7 million in 1817 and tolls covered the state's construction debt within the first year. It was enlarged several times, and from 1905 to 1918 most of the old line was replaced by the New York State Barge Canal.
routes.story: On opening day Governor DeWitt Clinton rode a canal boat from Buffalo to New York and poured a keg of Lake Erie water into the Atlantic, the 'Wedding of the Waters'. After that, mule-towed boats carried western grain east and settlers west.

facts.Towing: mules and horses on the towpath

routes.name: New York to San Francisco via the Panama Canal
citations: David McCullough, The Path Between the Seas: The Creation of the Panama Canal, 1870-1914 (New York: Simon & Schuster, 1977)
routes.notes: The canal opened to traffic on 15 August 1914. Our line through the Windward Passage and up the Pacific coast.
routes.goods_source: general history; not from a cargo manifest
routes.citation: David McCullough, The Path Between the Seas: The Creation of the Panama Canal, 1870-1914 (New York: Simon & Schuster, 1977)
routes.history: The Panama Canal formally opened on 15 August 1914 with the transit of the cargo ship SS Ancon. It cut thousands of miles from the New York–San Francisco sea route, which before had to go around Cape Horn or through the Strait of Magellan. The United States ran the canal until Panama took full control at noon on 31 December 1999.
routes.story: The first official transit took place days after the First World War broke out in Europe, so the opening got little attention. The canal still changed coast-to-coast American shipping almost at once.

facts.Route drawn: New York – Colón – Panama – San Francisco (reconstruction)
